purpose: Freeze and validate the user-supported two-layer hypothesis that RCI9 local reversal is the timing trigger and EMA20/30/40 directional ordering is the primary direction-permission context, without using trade outcomes or further same-window threshold optimization.

user_hypothesis.interpretation: RCI9 likely determines timing while EMA20/30/40 ordering likely determines allowed direction

candidate_kernel_priority.directional_kernel: state_before == IDLE AND rci9_turn_up == True AND ema_alignment == BULLISH_STACK
candidate_kernel_priority.support_observed: Combined scope: RCI9 turn-up 8/9; bullish stack 8/9; combined pair 7/9 with 2 controls. XAUUSD bullish stack 6/6.
secondary_diagnostics: EMA slope, spread/compression, and price location diagnostics

candidate_kernel_priority.directional_kernel: state_before == IDLE AND rci9_turn_down == True AND ema_alignment == BEARISH_STACK
candidate_kernel_priority.support_observed: Combined scope: RCI9 turn-down 10/10; all 10 observed primary SHORT events had bearish EMA stack. Exact false-positive reduction of the combined pair must be audited.
secondary_diagnostics: EMA slope, spread/compression, and price location diagnostics

candidate_kernel_priority.reason: Opposite RCI upper extreme was the stable exit signature, but exact secondary condition differs by scope. EMA ordering is not assumed for EXIT without separate evidence.
Opposite RCI lower extreme was the stable exit signature, but two of ten combined events were missed by the best strict pair. EMA ordering is not assumed for EXIT without separate evidence.

required_primary_comparisons: CORE-L0 versus KERNEL-L1 event recall and no-event false positives
CORE-S0 versus KERNEL-S1 event recall and no-event false positives
Every genuine primary event where EMA ordering is mixed or opposite
Every no-event boundary where EMA ordering is correct but RCI9 does not turn
Whether EMA ordering alone, slope, spread/compression, or price relative to EMA20/40 explains residual false positives
Cross-symbol stability between BTCUSD and XAUUSD

reentry_policy.REENTRY_LONG: DO_NOT_FREEZE_RULE; only one combined event and zero XAUUSD positives
reentry_policy.REENTRY_SHORT: OBSERVE_ONLY; four combined events and one XAUUSD event are insufficient
reentry_policy.ema_alignment_assumption: DO_NOT_COPY_PRIMARY EMA RULE TO REENTRY WITHOUT EVIDENCE

m7b_required_outputs: Frozen candidate-rule manifest with separate CORE and RCI9-plus-EMA kernel IDs and no trade-outcome fields
No-event false-positive table and clustering by ticker/time
Per-ticker cross-check showing which core signatures survive BTCUSD/XAUUSD separation
Leave-one-event-out or equivalent sensitivity audit for threshold dependence
EMA ordering residual audit: mixed/opposite genuine events and aligned no-event controls
Explicit list of rules rejected as one-sample or scope-specific artifacts
PASS/BLOCKED decision for prospective M7C shadow reproduction
m7b_guardrails: Do not use M6A/M6B/M6C returns, MFE, MAE, win/loss, or EXIT profitability to select trigger conditions.
Do not use alert-bar high, low, or close.
Use only the last fully closed M15 bar and the new M15 open available at decision time.
Do not treat pre-collector history as verified no-alert data.
Do not claim exact proprietary formula reconstruction.
Do not assume EMA ordering is sufficient; explicitly test slope, spread/compression, and price location as residual diagnostics.
Do not assume the primary-entry EMA rule also applies to EXIT or reentry.
Do not approve historical full-scan, cross-timeframe extraction, entry gates, alerts, orders, live readiness, or final signals.
Preserve source event identity from Webhook/SQLite; chart label redraw is not required for reentries.
after_m7b: M7C prospective shadow reproduction against newly collected genuine alerts
Only after M7C stability: historical candidate extraction on full CSV as independent proxy candidates
Only after historical audit: M5/H1 and other timeframe mapping with timeframe-specific recalculation and validation
